name: Microsoft Entra ID
summary: The directory behind every Microsoft 365 login, formerly Azure Active Directory: accounts and groups, single sign-on to other apps, multi-factor sign-in and access rules tied to managed devices.

factors: Every Microsoft 365 service signs in through it, so it is the last part you can switch off
Other software is wired to it one app at a time, over SAML, OpenID Connect and SCIM
Windows sign-in, device enrolment and Conditional Access rules depend on it and on Intune
Passwords and multi-factor registrations cannot be exported: everyone enrols again
Joiner and leaver routines that rely on the groups and licences assigned here

export.summary: Users, groups and the list of connected apps can be downloaded or read through Microsoft Graph. Credentials cannot: no password hashes and no authenticator registrations. Each app's sign-on settings have to be recreated by hand on the new side.

methods.name: Download users and groups
methods.detail: In the Entra admin centre, the Users and Groups lists have a bulk download that produces CSV files. That is enough to create the same accounts somewhere else.

methods.name: Microsoft Graph
methods.detail: The Graph API and its PowerShell module list users, group memberships, enterprise applications and their sign-on settings. Use it to build the inventory of everything that depends on Entra.

caveats: Find every app that signs in with Microsoft first: the Enterprise applications list and the sign-in logs show them
While any Microsoft 365 service remains, Entra stays underneath it. Your domain can be federated to the new provider so that people have one login, but Entra itself goes last
If you still run an on-premises Active Directory, point the new identity provider at that and most accounts need no migration
Entra-joined Windows PCs need a plan of their own: an identity provider does not manage devices
Keep one emergency admin account that does not depend on the new system

paths.verdict: The safe long-term choice when you have someone to run it: nothing is held back for a paid edition, and it can sit in front of an existing Active Directory.

import.summary: There is no importer for Entra. Create users from the CSV download or through the admin API, or connect Keycloak to an on-premises Active Directory if you have one. Then reconnect each app, one at a time, and have people set a new password and second factor at first sign-in.

transfers: User accounts and group memberships, from the export
Single sign-on to apps that speak SAML or OpenID Connect, once each is reconnected
Sign-in against an existing Active Directory, if you keep one
lost: Passwords and authenticator registrations: everyone enrols again
Conditional Access rules based on device compliance
Windows sign-in and device management through Entra and Intune
Automatic account creation in other apps, unless you add a SCIM extension

paths.verdict: The most approachable to run for a small company, and it can front older apps that never learned single sign-on. Check which features sit in the paid edition.

import.summary: No importer for Entra here either. Create users from the CSV download or through the API, or sync them from an on-premises Active Directory. Reconnect each app in turn; software without single sign-on can go behind its proxy. Everyone sets a new password and second factor.

transfers: User accounts and group memberships, from the export
Single sign-on to apps that speak SAML or OpenID Connect, once each is reconnected
Automatic account creation and removal in apps that accept SCIM
lost: Passwords and authenticator registrations: everyone enrols again
Conditional Access rules based on device compliance, outside the paid edition
Windows sign-in and device management through Entra and Intune

paths.verdict: Worth a look if you would rather not run the login server at all: the developers' hosted service removes the hardest part. Strongest where your apps speak OpenID Connect.

import.summary: No importer for Entra. Create users in the console or through its API; password hashes cannot come out of Entra, so people set new ones. Reconnect each app in turn.

transfers: User accounts, recreated from the export
Single sign-on to apps that speak OpenID Connect or SAML, once each is reconnected
Passkeys and multi-factor, after people enrol again
lost: Passwords and authenticator registrations: everyone enrols again
Continuous sync from an Active Directory
Conditional Access rules based on device compliance
Windows sign-in and device management through Entra and Intune
Automatic account creation in other apps
